title: std::basic_filebuf
summary: std::basic_filebuf is a std::basic_streambuf whose associated character sequence is a file. Both the input sequence and the output sequence are associated with the same file, and a joint file position is maintained for both operations.

title: std::basic_filebuf<CharT,Traits>::basic_filebuf
summary: Constructs new std::basic_filebuf object.

title: std::basic_filebuf<CharT,Traits>::close
summary: If a put area exist (e.g. file was opened for writing), first calls overflow(Traits::eof()) to write all pending output to the file, including any unshift sequences.

title: std::basic_filebuf<CharT,Traits>::imbue
summary: Changes the associated locale so that all characters inserted or extracted after this call (and until another call to imbue()) are converted using the std::codecvt facet of loc.

title: std::basic_filebuf<CharT,Traits>::is_open
summary: Returns true if the most recent call to open() succeeded and there has been no call to close() since then.

title: std::basic_filebuf<CharT,Traits>::native_handle
summary: Returns the implementation defined underlying handle associated with *this. The behavior is undefined if is_open() is false.

title: std::basic_filebuf<CharT,Traits>::open
summary: If the associated file was already open (is_open() != false), returns a null pointer right away.

title: std::basic_filebuf<CharT,Traits>::operator=
summary: Assigns another basic_filebuf object.

title: std::basic_filebuf<CharT,Traits>::overflow
summary: Writes some data from the put area to the associated character sequence (to the file).

title: std::basic_filebuf<CharT,Traits>::pbackfail
summary: This protected virtual function is called by the public functions basic_streambuf::sungetc and basic_streambuf::sputbackc (which, in turn, are called by basic_istream::unget and basic_istream::putback).

title: std::basic_filebuf<CharT,Traits>::seekoff
summary: Repositions the file pointer, if possible, to the position that corresponds to exactly off characters from beginning, end, or current position of the file (depending on the value of dir).

title: std::basic_filebuf<CharT,Traits>::seekpos
summary: Repositions the file pointer, if possible, to the position indicated by sp. If the associated file is not open (is_open() == false), fails immediately.

title: std::basic_filebuf<CharT,Traits>::setbuf
summary: If s is a null pointer and n is zero, the filebuf becomes unbuffered for output, meaning pbase() and pptr() are null and any output is immediately sent to file.

title: std::basic_filebuf<CharT,Traits>::showmanyc
summary: If implemented, returns the number of characters left to read from the file.

title: std::basic_filebuf<CharT,Traits>::swap
summary: Swaps the state and the contents of *this and rhs.

title: std::swap(std::basic_filebuf)
summary: Overloads the std::swap algorithm for std::basic_filebuf. Exchanges the state of lhs with that of rhs. Effectively calls lhs.swap(rhs).

title: std::basic_filebuf<CharT,Traits>::sync
summary: If a put area exists (e.g. the file was opened for writing), calls overflow() to write all pending output to the file, then flushes the file as if by calling std::fflush.

title: std::basic_filebuf<CharT,Traits>::uflow
summary: Behaves like the underflow(), except that if underflow() succeeds (does not return Traits::eof()), then advances the next pointer for the get area.

title: std::basic_filebuf<CharT,Traits>::underflow
summary: Reads more data into the input area.

title: std::basic_filebuf<CharT,Traits>::~basic_filebuf
summary: Calls close() to close the associated file and destructs all other members of basic_filebuf. If an exception occurs during the destruction of the object, including the call to close(), it is caught and not rethrown.

summary: A LegacyBidirectionalIterator is a LegacyForwardIterator that can be moved in both directions (i.e. incremented and decremented).

title: C++ named requirements: BinaryPredicate
summary: BinaryPredicate is a set of requirements expected by some of the standard library facilities from the user-provided arguments.

title: C++ named requirements: BinaryTypeTrait (since C++11)
summary: A BinaryTypeTrait is a class template that describes a relationship between its two template type parameters with a std::integral_constant (typically std::bool_constant) specialization.

title: C++ named requirements: BitmaskType
summary: Defines a type that can be used to represent a set of constant values or any combination of those values.

title: C++ named requirements: BooleanTestable
summary: Specifies that an expression of such a type and value category is convertible to bool, and for which the logical operators for the type or two different BooleanTestable types have the usual behavior (including short-circuiting).

title: C++ named requirements: Callable
summary: A Callable type is a type for which the INVOKE and INVOKE<R> operations (used by, e.g., std::function, std::bind, and std::thread::thread) are applicable.

title: C++ named requirements: CharTraits
summary: CharTraits is a traits class that abstracts basic character and string operations for a given character type.

title: C++ named requirements: Clock (since C++11)
summary: The Clock requirements describe a bundle consisting of a std::chrono::duration, a std::chrono::time_point, and a function now() to get the current time_point.

title: C++ named requirements: Compare
summary: Compare is a set of requirements expected by some of the standard library facilities from the user-provided function object types.

title: C++ named requirements: ConstexprIterator (since C++20)
summary: A ConstexprIterator is a LegacyIterator that can be used during constant expression evaluation.

title: C++ named requirements: Container
summary: A Container is an object used to store other objects and taking care of the management of the memory used by the objects it contains.

title: C++ named requirements: ContiguousContainer (since C++17)
summary: A ContiguousContainer is a Container that stores objects in contiguous memory locations.

title: C++ named requirements: LegacyContiguousIterator (since C++17)
summary: A LegacyContiguousIterator is a LegacyIterator whose logically adjacent elements are also physically adjacent in memory.

title: C++ named requirements: CopyAssignable
summary: Specifies that an instance of the type can be copy-assigned from an lvalue expression.

title: C++ named requirements: CopyConstructible
summary: Specifies that an instance of the type can be copy-constructed from an lvalue expression.

title: C++ named requirements: CopyInsertable (since C++11)
summary: Specifies that an object of the type can be copy-constructed in-place by a given allocator.

title: C++ named requirements: DefaultConstructible
summary: Specifies that an instance of the type can be default constructed.

title: C++ named requirements: DefaultInsertable (since C++11)
summary: Specifies that an object of the type can be default-constructed in-place by a given allocator.

title: C++ named requirements: Destructible
summary: Specifies that an instance of the type can be destructed.

title: C++ named requirements: EmplaceConstructible (since C++11)
summary: Specifies that an object of the type can be constructed from a given set of arguments in uninitialized storage by a given allocator.

title: C++ named requirements: EqualityComparable
summary: The type must work with == operator and the result should have standard semantics.

title: C++ named requirements: Erasable (since C++11)
summary: Specifies that an object of the type can be destroyed by a given Allocator.

title: C++ named requirements: FormattedInputFunction
summary: A FormattedInputFunction is a stream input function that performs the following:

title: C++ named requirements: FormattedOutputFunction
summary: A FormattedOutputFunction is a stream output function that performs the following:

title: C++ named requirements: Formatter (since C++20)
summary: Formatter is a type that abstracts formatting operations for a given formatting argument type and character type.

title: C++ named requirements: LegacyForwardIterator
summary: A LegacyForwardIterator is a LegacyIterator that can read data from the pointed-to element.

title: C++ named requirements: FunctionObject
summary: A FunctionObject type is the type of an object that can be used on the left of the function call operator.

title: C++ named requirements: Hash (since C++11)
summary: A Hash is a function object for which the output depends only on the input and has a very low probability of yielding the same output given different input values.

title: C++ named requirements: ImplicitLifetimeType
summary: Note: the standard doesn't define a named requirement with this name. This is a type category defined by the core language.

title: C++ named requirements: LegacyInputIterator
summary: A LegacyInputIterator is a LegacyIterator that can read from the pointed-to element.

title: C++ named requirements: LegacyIterator
summary: The LegacyIterator requirements describe types that can be used to identify and traverse the elements of a container.

title: C++ named requirements: LayoutMapping (since C++23)
summary: LayoutMapping controls the mapping of a multidimensional index to a one-dimensional offset to data handle in std::mdspan.

title: C++ named requirements: LayoutMappingPolicy (since C++23)
summary: LayoutMappingPolicy is a type used to specify layout policy of std::mdspan. It provides a member alias template whose specialization is a LayoutMapping type.

title: C++ named requirements: LessThanComparable
summary: The type must work with < operator and the result should have standard semantics.

title: C++ named requirements: LiteralType (since C++11)
summary: Specifies that a type is a literal type. Literal types are the types of constexpr variables and they can be constructed, manipulated, and returned from constexpr functions.

title: C++ named requirements: Lockable (since C++11)
summary: The Lockable requirements extends the BasicLockable requirements to include attempted locking.

title: C++ named requirements: MoveAssignable (since C++11)
summary: Specifies that an instance of the type can be assigned from an rvalue argument.

title: C++ named requirements: MoveConstructible (since C++11)
summary: Specifies that an instance of the type can be constructed from an rvalue argument.

title: C++ named requirements: MoveInsertable (since C++11)
summary: Specifies that an object of the type can be constructed into uninitialized storage from an rvalue of that type by a given allocator.

title: C++ named requirements: Mutex (since C++11)
summary: The Mutex requirements extends the Lockable requirements to include inter-thread synchronization.

title: C++ named requirements: NullablePointer (since C++11)
summary: Specifies that the type is a pointer-like object which can be compared to std::nullptr_t objects.

title: C++ named requirements: NumericType
summary: Specifies that the type can be used as the template argument of std::valarray.

title: C++ named requirements: LegacyOutputIterator
summary: A LegacyOutputIterator is a LegacyIterator that can write to the pointed-to element.

title: C++ named requirements: PODType (deprecated in C++20)
summary: Specifies that the type is POD (Plain Old Data) type. This means the type is compatible with the types used in the C programming language, that is, can be exchanged with C libraries directly, in its binary form.

title: C++ named requirements: Predicate
summary: The Predicate requirements describe a callable that returns a BooleanTestable value.

title: C++ named requirements: LegacyRandomAccessIterator
summary: A LegacyRandomAccessIterator is a LegacyBidirectionalIterator that can be moved to point to any element in constant time.

title: C++ named requirements: RandomNumberDistribution (since C++11)
summary: A RandomNumberDistribution is a function object returning random numbers according to a probability density function p(x) or a discrete probability distribution P(xi).

title: C++ named requirements: RandomNumberEngine (since C++11)
summary: A random number engine is a function object returning unsigned integer values such that each value in the range of possible results has (ideally) equal probability.

title: C++ named requirements: RandomNumberEngineAdaptor (since C++11)
summary: A RandomNumberEngineAdaptor is a RandomNumberEngine that transforms the output of another RandomNumberEngine, the latter of which is termed a base engine.

title: C++ named requirements: RangeAdaptorClosureObject (since C++20)
summary: Range adaptor closure objects are FunctionObjects that are callable via the pipe operator: if C is a range adaptor closure object and R is a range, these two expressions are equivalent:

title: C++ named requirements: RangeAdaptorObject (since C++20)
summary: Range adaptor objects are customization point objects that accept viewable_range as their first arguments and return a view.

title: C++ named requirements: RegexTraits (since C++11)
summary: RegexTraits is a traits class that abstracts operations needed for a given character type when as template type parameters for std::basic_regex.

title: C++ named requirements: ReversibleContainer
summary: A ReversibleContainer is a Container that has iterators that meet the requirements of either LegacyBidirectionalIterator or LegacyRandomAccessIterator.

title: C++ named requirements: ScalarType
summary: Note: the standard doesn't define a named requirement with this name. This is a type category defined by the core language.

title: C++ named requirements: SeedSequence (since C++11)
summary: A SeedSequence is an object that produces unsigned integer values i in the range 0 ≤ i < 232 based on a consumed range of integer data.

title: C++ named requirements: SequenceContainer
summary: A SequenceContainer is a Container that stores objects of the same type in a linear arrangement.

title: C++ named requirements: SharedLockable (since C++14)
summary: The SharedLockable requirements describe the minimal characteristics of types that provide shared blocking semantics for execution agents (i.e. threads).

title: C++ named requirements: SharedMutex (since C++17)
summary: The SharedMutex requirements extend the Mutex requirements to include shared lock ownership mode.

title: C++ named requirements: SharedTimedLockable (since C++14)
summary: The SharedTimedLockable requirements describe the characteristics of types that provide timed shared blocking semantics for execution agents (threads, processes, tasks).

title: C++ named requirements: SharedTimedMutex (since C++14)
summary: The SharedTimedMutex requirements extend the TimedMutex requirements to include shared lock ownership mode.

title: C++ named requirements: StandardLayoutType (since C++11)
summary: Specifies that a type is a standard layout type. Standard layout types are useful for communicating with code written in other programming languages.

title: C++ named requirements: Swappable
summary: Any lvalue or rvalue of this type can be swapped with any lvalue or rvalue of some other type, using unqualified function call swap() in the context where both std::swap and the user-defined swap()s are visible.

title: C++ named requirements: TimedLockable (since C++11)
summary: The TimedLockable requirements describe the characteristics of types that provide timed exclusive blocking semantics for execution agents (threads, processes, tasks).

title: C++ named requirements: TimedMutex (since C++11)
summary: The TimedMutex requirements extend the TimedLockable requirements to include inter-thread synchronization.

title: C++ named requirements: TransformationTrait (since C++11)
summary: A TransformationTrait is a class template that provides a transformation of its template type parameter.

title: C++ named requirements: TrivialClock (since C++11)
summary: The TrivialClock requirements describe the requirements satisfied by several clocks in the chrono library.

title: C++ named requirements: TriviallyCopyable (since C++11)
summary: Note: the standard doesn't define a named requirement with this name. This is a type category defined by the core language.

title: C++ named requirements: TrivialType (since C++11)(deprecated in C++26)
summary: Specifies that a type is a trivial type.

title: C++ named requirements: UnaryTypeTrait (since C++11)
summary: A UnaryTypeTrait is a class template that describes a property of its template type parameter with an std::integral_constant (typically std::bool_constant) specialization.

title: C++ named requirements: UnformattedInputFunction
summary: An UnformattedInputFunction is a stream input function that performs the following:

title: C++ named requirements: UnformattedOutputFunction
summary: A UnformattedOutputFunction is a stream output function that performs the following:

title: C++ named requirements: UniformRandomBitGenerator (since C++11)
summary: A uniform random bit generator is a function object returning unsigned integer values such that each value in the range of possible results has (ideally) equal probability.

title: C++ named requirements: UnorderedAssociativeContainer (since C++11)
summary: Unordered associative containers are Containers that provide fast lookup of objects based on keys. Worst case complexity is linear but on average much faster for most of the operations.

title: C++ named requirements: ValueSwappable (since C++11)
summary: Two objects of this type can be dereferenced and the resulting values can be swapped using unqualified function call swap() in the context where both std::swap and the user-defined swap()s are visible.

title: Numerics library
summary: The C++ numerics library includes common mathematical functions and types, as well as optimized numeric arrays and support for random number generation.

title: std::add_sat
summary: Computes the saturating addition x + y. This operation (unlike built-in arithmetic operations on integers) behaves as-if it is a mathematical operation with an infinite range.

title: std::bit_cast
summary: Obtain a value of type To by reinterpreting the object representation of From. Every bit in the value representation of the returned To object is equal to the corresponding bit in the object representation of from.

title: std::bit_ceil
summary: Calculates the smallest integral power of two that is not smaller than x.

title: std::bit_floor
summary: If x is not zero, calculates the largest integral power of two that is not greater than x. If x is zero, returns zero.

title: std::bit_width
summary: If x is not zero, calculates the number of bits needed to store the value x, that is, 1 + floor(log2(x)). If x is zero, returns zero.

title: std::byteswap
summary: Reverses the bytes in the given integer value n.

title: std::acosh(std::complex)
summary: Computes complex arc hyperbolic cosine of a complex value z with branch cut at values less than 1 along the real axis.

title: std::asinh(std::complex)

summary: Computes complex arc tangent of a complex value z. Branch cut exists outside the interval [−i, +i] along the imaginary axis.

summary: Compute base-e exponential of z, that is e (Euler's number, 2.7182818) raised to the z power.

summary: Computes complex common (base 10) logarithm of a complex value z with a branch cut along the negative real axis.

summary: The norm calculated by this function is also known as field norm or absolute square.

summary: Assigns new values to the contents.

title: std::complex<T>::operator+(unary), operator-(unary)
summary: Implements the analogs of the unary arithmetic operators for complex numbers.

title: operator+,-,*,/ (std::complex)
summary: Implements the binary operators for complex arithmetic and for mixed complex/scalar arithmetic. Scalar arguments are treated as complex numbers with the real part equal to the argument and the imaginary part set to zero.

title: operator==,!=(std::complex)
summary: Compares two complex numbers. Scalar arguments are treated as complex numbers with the real part equal to the argument and the imaginary part set to zero.

title: operator<<,>>(std::complex)
summary: May throw std::ios_base::failure on stream errors.

title: std::polar(std::complex)
summary: Returns a complex number with magnitude r and phase angle theta.

summary: Overload (1) was provided in C++98 to match the extra overloads (2) of std::pow. Those overloads were removed by the resolution of LWG issue 550, and overload (1) was removed by the resolution of LWG issue 844.

title: std::tan(std::complex)
summary: Computes complex tangent of a complex value z.

title: std::tanh(std::complex)
summary: Computes complex hyperbolic tangent of a complex value z.

title: Mathematical constants
summary: A program that instantiates a primary template of a mathematical constant variable template is ill-formed.

title: std::countl_one
summary: Returns the number of consecutive 1 ("one") bits in the value of x, starting from the most significant bit ("left").

title: std::countl_zero
summary: Returns the number of consecutive 0 bits in the value of x, starting from the most significant bit ("left").

title: std::countr_one
summary: Returns the number of consecutive 1 bits in the value of x, starting from the least significant bit ("right").

title: std::countr_zero
summary: Returns the number of consecutive 0 bits in the value of x, starting from the least significant bit ("right").

title: std::div_sat
summary: Computes the saturating division x / y. If T is a signed integer type, x is the smallest (most negative) value of T, and y == -1, returns the greatest value of T; otherwise, returns x / y.

title: Floating-point environment (since C++11)
summary: The floating-point environment is the set of floating-point status flags and control modes supported by the implementation.

title: FE_DFL_ENV
summary: The macro constant FE_DFL_ENV expands to an expression of type const std::fenv_t*, which points to a full copy of the default floating-point environment, that is, the environment as loaded at program startup.

title: FE_DIVBYZERO, FE_INEXACT, FE_INVALID, FE_OVERFLOW, FE_UNDERFLOW, FE_ALL_EXCEPT
summary: All these macro constants (except FE_ALL_EXCEPT) expand to integer constant expressions that are distinct powers of 2, which uniquely identify all supported floating-point exceptions.

title: FE_DOWNWARD, FE_TONEAREST, FE_TOWARDZERO, FE_UPWARD
summary: Each of these macro constants expands to a nonnegative integer constant expression, which can be used with std::fesetround and std::fegetround to indicate one of the supported floating-point rounding modes.

title: std::feclearexcept
summary: Attempts to clear the floating-point exceptions that are listed in the bitmask argument excepts, which is a bitwise OR of the floating point exception macros.

title: std::fegetenv, std::fesetenv
summary: Manages the status of the floating-point environment.

title: std::fegetexceptflag, std::fesetexceptflag
summary: 1) Attempts to obtain the full contents of the floating-point exception flags that are listed in the bitmask argument excepts, which is a bitwise OR of the floating point exception macros.

title: std::feholdexcept

title: std::feraiseexcept
summary: Attempts to raise all floating point exceptions listed in excepts (a bitwise OR of the floating point exception macros). If one of the exceptions is FE_OVERFLOW or FE_UNDERFLOW, this function may additionally raise FE_INEXACT.

title: std::fegetround, std::fesetround
summary: Manages the floating-point rounding direction.

title: std::fetestexcept
summary: Determines which of the specified subset of the floating point exceptions are currently set. The argument excepts is a bitwise OR of the floating point exception macros.

title: std::feupdateenv
summary: First, remembers the currently raised floating-point exceptions, then restores the floating-point environment from the object pointed to by envp (similar to std::fesetenv), then raises the floating-point exceptions that were saved.

title: std::gcd
summary: Computes the greatest common divisor of the integers m and n.

title: std::has_single_bit
summary: Checks if x is an integral power of two.

title: std::lcm
summary: Computes the least common multiple of the integers m and n.

title: std::lerp
summary: a + t(b − a)

title: Basic linear algebra algorithms (since C++26)
summary: Basic linear algebra algorithms are based on the dense Basic Linear Algebra Subroutines (BLAS) which corresponds to a subset of the BLAS Standard.

title: std::abs, std::labs, std::llabs, std::imaxabs
summary: Computes the absolute value of the integer number num. The behavior is undefined if the result cannot be represented by the return type.

title: std::acos, std::acosf, std::acosl
summary: If no errors occur, the arc cosine of num (arccos(num)) in the range [0, π], is returned.

title: std::acosh, std::acoshf, std::acoshl
summary: If no errors occur, the inverse hyperbolic cosine of num (cosh-1(num), or arcosh(num)) on the interval [0, +∞], is returned.

title: std::asin, std::asinf, std::asinl
summary: If a domain error occurs, an implementation-defined value is returned (NaN where supported).

title: std::asinh, std::asinhf, std::asinhl
summary: If no errors occur, the inverse hyperbolic sine of num (sinh-1(num), or arsinh(num)), is returned.

title: std::atan, std::atanf, std::atanl
summary: If a range error occurs due to underflow, the correct result (after rounding) is returned.

title: std::atan2, std::atan2f, std::atan2l
summary: If a domain error occurs, an implementation-defined value is returned (NaN where supported).

title: std::atanh, std::atanhf, std::atanhl
summary: If no errors occur, the inverse hyperbolic tangent of num (tanh-1(num), or artanh(num)), is returned.

title: std::cbrt, std::cbrtf, std::cbrtl
summary: If no errors occur, the cube root of num (3√num), is returned.

title: std::ceil, std::ceilf, std::ceill
summary: If no errors occur, the smallest integer value not less than num, that is ⌈num⌉, is returned.

title: std::copysign, std::copysignf, std::copysignl
summary: If no errors occur, the floating point value with the magnitude of mag and the sign of sgn is returned.

title: std::cos, std::cosf, std::cosl
summary: If no errors occur, the cosine of num (cos(num)) in the range [-1.0, +1.0], is returned.

title: std::cosh, std::coshf, std::coshl
summary: If a range error due to overflow occurs, +HUGE_VAL, +HUGE_VALF, or +HUGE_VALL is returned.

title: std::div, std::ldiv, std::lldiv, std::imaxdiv
summary: Computes both the quotient and the remainder of the division of the numerator x by the denominator y.

title: std::erf, std::erff, std::erfl
summary: Errors are reported as specified in math_errhandling.

title: std::erfc, std::erfcf, std::erfcl
summary: If a range error occurs due to underflow, the correct result (after rounding) is returned.

title: std::exp, std::expf, std::expl
summary: If no errors occur, the base-e exponential of num (enum) is returned.

title: std::exp2, std::exp2f, std::exp2l
summary: If no errors occur, the base-2 exponential of num (2num) is returned.

title: std::expm1, std::expm1f, std::expm1l
summary: If no errors occur enum-1 is returned.

title: std::abs(float), std::fabs, std::fabsf, std::fabsl

title: std::fdim, std::fdimf, std::fdiml
summary: If successful, returns the positive difference between x and y.

title: std::floor, std::floorf, std::floorl
summary: If no errors occur, the largest integer value not greater than num, that is ⌊num⌋, is returned.

title: std::fma, std::fmaf, std::fmal
summary: If successful, returns the value of x * y + z as if calculated to infinite precision and rounded once to fit the result type (or, alternatively, calculated as a single ternary floating-point operation).

title: std::fmax, std::fmaxf, std::fmaxl
summary: If successful, returns the larger of two floating point values. The value returned is exact and does not depend on any rounding modes.

title: std::fmin, std::fminf, std::fminl
summary: If successful, returns the smaller of two floating point values. The value returned is exact and does not depend on any rounding modes.

title: std::fmod, std::fmodf, std::fmodl
summary: The floating-point remainder of the division operation x / y calculated by this function is exactly the value x - iquot * y, where iquot is x / y with its fractional part truncated.

title: FP_NORMAL, FP_SUBNORMAL, FP_ZERO, FP_INFINITE, FP_NAN
summary: The FP_NORMAL, FP_SUBNORMAL, FP_ZERO, FP_INFINITE, FP_NAN macros each represent a distinct category of floating-point numbers.

title: std::fpclassify
summary: one of FP_INFINITE, FP_NAN, FP_NORMAL, FP_SUBNORMAL, FP_ZERO or implementation-defined type, specifying the category of num.

title: std::frexp, std::frexpf, std::frexpl
summary: If num is zero, returns zero and stores zero in *exp.

title: HUGE_VALF, HUGE_VAL, HUGE_VALL
summary: The macros HUGE_VALF, HUGE_VAL and HUGE_VALL macros expand to positive floating point constant expressions which compare equal to the values returned by floating-point functions and operators in case of overflow (see math_errhandling).

title: std::isless

title: std::abort
summary: Causes abnormal program termination unless SIGABRT is being caught by a signal handler passed to std::signal and the handler does not return.

title: std::at_quick_exit
summary: Registers the function pointed to by func to be called on quick program termination (via std::quick_exit).

title: std::atexit
summary: Registers the function pointed to by func to be called on normal program termination (via std::exit() or returning from the main function)

title: std::exit
summary: Causes normal program termination to occur.

title: EXIT_SUCCESS, EXIT_FAILURE
summary: The EXIT_SUCCESS and EXIT_FAILURE macros expand into integral constant expressions that can be used as arguments to the std::exit function (and, therefore, as the values to return from the main function), and indicate program execution…

title: std::getenv
summary: Searches the environment list provided by the host environment (the OS), for a string that matches the C string pointed to by env_var and returns a pointer to the C string that is associated with the matched environment list member.

title: std::jmp_buf
summary: The std::jmp_buf type is an array type suitable for storing information to restore a calling environment. The stored information is sufficient to restore execution at the correct block of the program and invocation of that block.

title: std::longjmp
summary: Loads the execution context env saved by a previous call to setjmp. This function does not return. Control is transferred to the call site of the macro setjmp that set up env.

title: std::quick_exit
summary: Causes normal program termination to occur without completely cleaning the resources.

title: std::raise
summary: Sends signal sig to the program. The signal handler (specified using the std::signal() function) is invoked.

title: setjmp
summary: Saves the current execution context into a variable env of type std::jmp_buf. This variable can later be used to restore the current execution context by std::longjmp function.

title: std::sig_atomic_t
summary: An integer type which can be accessed as an atomic entity even in the presence of asynchronous interrupts made by signals.

title: SIG_ERR
summary: A value of type void (*)(int). When returned by std::signal, indicates that an error has occurred.

title: SIG_DFL, SIG_IGN
summary: The SIG_DFL and SIG_IGN macros expand into integral expressions that are not equal to an address of any function. The macros define signal handling strategies for std::signal() function.

title: SIGTERM, SIGSEGV, SIGINT, SIGILL, SIGABRT, SIGFPE
summary: Each of the above macro constants expands to an integer constant expression with distinct values, which represent different signals sent to the program.

title: std::signal
summary: Changes handling of the signal sig. Depending on handler, the signal can be ignored, set to default, or handled by a user-defined function.

title: std::system
summary: Calls the host environment's command processor (e.g. /bin/sh, cmd.exe) with the parameter command. Returns an implementation-defined value (usually the value that the invoked program returns).

title: std::source_location
summary: The std::source_location class represents certain information about the source code, such as file names, line numbers, and function names.

title: std::source_location::column
summary: Returns an implementation-defined value representing some offset from the start of the line represented by this object (i.e., the column number).

title: std::source_location::current
summary: Constructs a new source_location object corresponding to the location of the call site.

title: std::source_location::file_name
summary: Returns the name of the current source file represented by this object, represented as a null-terminated byte string.

title: std::source_location::function_name
summary: Returns the name of the function associated with the position represented by this object, if any.

title: std::source_location::line
summary: Returns the line number represented by this object.

title: std::stacktrace_entry
summary: The stacktrace_entry class provides operations for querying information about an evaluation in a stacktrace. Each stacktrace_entry object is either empty, or represents an evaluation in a stacktrace.

title: std::stacktrace_entry::description
summary: Returns a description of the evaluation represented by *this on success, or an empty string on failure other than allocation failure, e.g. when *this is empty.

title: std::formatter<std::stacktrace_entry>
summary: The template specialization of std::formatter for std::stacktrace_entry allows users to convert a stacktrace entry object to string using formatting functions such as std::format.

title: std::hash<std::stacktrace_entry>
summary: The template specialization of std::hash for std::stacktrace_entry allows users to obtain hashes of values of type std::stacktrace_entry.

title: std::stacktrace_entry::native_handle
summary: Returns the implementation-defined underlying native handle. Successive invocations of this function for an unchanged stacktrace_entry object return identical values.

title: std::stacktrace_entry::operator=
summary: Copy assignment operator. Replaces the contents of *this with those of other.

title: std::stacktrace_entry::operator bool
summary: Checks whether the stacktrace_entry is non-empty, i.e. it represents an evaluation in a stacktrace.

title: operator==, operator<=>(std::stacktrace_entry)
summary: These functions are not visible to ordinary unqualified or qualified lookup, and can only be found by argument-dependent lookup when std::stacktrace_entry is an associated class of the arguments.

title: std::operator<<(std::stacktrace_entry)
summary: Inserts the description of f into the output stream os. Equivalent to return os << std::to_string(f);.

title: std::stacktrace_entry::source_file
summary: Returns the presumed or actual name of the source file that lexically contains the expression or statement whose evaluation is represented by *this, or an empty string on failure other than allocation failure, e.g. when *this is empty.

title: std::stacktrace_entry::source_line
summary: Returns a 1-based line number that lexically relates to the evaluation represented by *this, or 0 on failure other than allocation failure, e.g. when *this is empty.

title: std::stacktrace_entry::stacktrace_entry
summary: A non-empty stacktrace_entry can be obtained from a std::basic_stacktrace created by std::basic_stacktrace::current or a copy of such std::basic_stacktrace.

title: std::to_string
summary: Returns a string with a description of f.

title: std::strong_order
summary: Compares two values using 3-way comparison and produces a result of type std::strong_ordering.

title: std::strong_ordering
summary: The class type std::strong_ordering is the result type of a three-way comparison that:

title: std::ranges::swap
summary: Exchanges the values referenced by t and u.

title: std::three_way_comparable, std::three_way_comparable_with
summary: __WeaklyEqualityComparableWith, __PartiallyOrderedWith, and __ComparisonCommonTypeWith are exposition-only concepts. See descriptions of equality_comparable and totally_ordered.

title: std::to_chars
summary: Converts value into a character string by successively filling the range [first, last), where [first, last) is required to be a valid range.

title: std::to_chars_result
summary: std::to_chars_result is the return type of std::to_chars. It has no base classes, and only has the following members.

title: std::to_underlying
summary: Converts an enumeration to its underlying type. Equivalent to return static_cast<std::underlying_type_t<Enum>>(e);.

title: std::tuple
summary: Class template std::tuple is a fixed-size collection of heterogeneous values. It is a generalization of std::pair.

title: std::basic_common_reference<tuple-like>
summary: The common reference type of two tuple-like types is a std::tuple consists of the common reference types of all corresponding element type pairs of both types, where the cv and reference qualifiers on the tuple-like types are applied to…

title: std::common_type<tuple-like>
summary: The common type of two tuple-like types is a std::tuple consists of the common types of all corresponding element type pairs of both types.

title: deduction guides for std::tuple
summary: These deduction guides are provided for std::tuple to account for the edge cases missed by the implicit deduction guides, in particular, non-copyable arguments and array to pointer conversion.

title: std::forward_as_tuple
summary: Constructs a tuple of references to the arguments in args suitable for forwarding as an argument to a function. The tuple has rvalue reference data members when rvalues are used as arguments, and otherwise has lvalue reference data members.

title: std::get(std::tuple)
summary: A reference to the selected element of t.

title: std::ignore
summary: A void expression or a volatile bit-field value cannot be assigned to std::ignore.

title: std::make_tuple
summary: Creates a tuple object, deducing the target type from the types of arguments.

title: std::tuple<Types...>::operator=
summary: Replaces the contents of the tuple with the contents of another tuple-like object.

title: operator==,!=,<,<=,>,>=,<=>(std::tuple)
summary: All comparison operators are short-circuited; they do not access tuple elements beyond what is necessary to determine the result of the comparison.

title: std::tuple<Types...>::swap
summary: Calls swap (which might be std::swap, or might be found via ADL) for each element in *this and its corresponding element in other.

title: std::swap(std::tuple)
summary: Swaps the contents of lhs and rhs. Equivalent to lhs.swap(rhs).

title: std::tie
summary: Creates a tuple of lvalue references to its arguments or instances of std::ignore.

title: std::tuple<Types...>::tuple
summary: Constructs a new tuple.

title: tuple-like, pair-like
summary: tuple-like types implement the tuple protocol, i.e., such types can be used with std::get, std::tuple_element and std::tuple_size.

title: std::tuple_cat
summary: Constructs a tuple that is a concatenation of all tuples in args.

title: std::tuple_element<std::tuple>
summary: Provides compile-time indexed access to the types of the elements of the tuple.

title: std::tuple_size<std::tuple>
summary: Provides access to the number of elements in a tuple as a compile-time constant expression.

title: std::uses_allocator<std::tuple>
summary: This specialization of std::uses_allocator informs other library components that tuples support uses-allocator construction, even though they do not have a nested allocator_type.

title: std::tuple_element
summary: Provides compile-time indexed access to the types of the elements of a tuple-like type.

title: std::tuple_size
summary: Provides access to the number of elements in a tuple-like type as a compile-time constant expression.

title: std::unreachable
summary: Invokes undefined behavior at a given point.

title: Variadic functions
summary: Variadic functions are functions (e.g. std::printf) which take a variable number of arguments.

title: va_arg
summary: The va_arg macro expands to an expression of type T that corresponds to the next parameter from the va_list ap.

title: va_copy
summary: The va_copy macro copies src to dest.

title: va_end
summary: The va_end macro performs cleanup for an ap object initialized by a call to va_start or va_copy. va_end may modify ap so that it is no longer usable.

title: std::va_list
summary: va_list is a complete object type (in practice, a unique built-in type or char*) suitable for holding the information needed by the macros va_start, va_copy, va_arg, and va_end.

title: va_start
summary: The va_start macro enables access to the variable arguments following the named argument parm_n.

title: std::variant
summary: The class template std::variant represents a type-safe union.

title: std::bad_variant_access
summary: std::bad_variant_access is the type of the exception thrown in the following situations:

title: std::variant<Types...>::emplace
summary: Creates a new value in-place, in an existing variant object

title: std::get(std::variant)
summary: Reference to the value stored in the variant.

title: std::get_if (std::variant)
summary: Pointer to the value stored in the pointed-to variant or null pointer on error.

title: std::hash<std::variant>
summary: The template specialization of std::hash for the std::variant template allows users to obtain hashes of variant objects.

title: std::holds_alternative
summary: Checks if the variant v holds the alternative T. The call is ill-formed if T does not appear exactly once in Types...

title: std::variant<Types...>::index
summary: Returns the zero-based index of the alternative that is currently held by the variant.

title: std::monostate
summary: Unit type intended for use as a well-behaved empty alternative in std::variant.

title: std::variant<Types...>::operator=
summary: Assigns a new value to an existing variant object.

title: operator==, !=, <, <=, >, >=, <=>(std::variant)
summary: Performs comparison operations on std::variant objects.

title: std::variant<Types...>::swap
summary: Swaps two variant objects.

title: std::swap(std::variant)
summary: Overloads the std::swap algorithm for std::variant. Effectively calls lhs.swap(rhs).

title: std::variant<Types...>::valueless_by_exception
summary: Returns false if and only if the variant holds a value.

title: std::variant<Types...>::variant
summary: Constructs a new variant object.

title: std::variant_alternative, std::variant_alternative_t
summary: Provides compile-time indexed access to the types of the alternatives of the possibly cv-qualified variant, combining cv-qualifications of the variant (if any) with the cv-qualifications of the alternative.

title: std::variant_npos
summary: This is a special value equal to the largest value representable by the type std::size_t, used as the return value of index() when valueless_by_exception() is true.

title: std::variant_size, std::variant_size_v
summary: Provides access to the number of alternatives in a possibly cv-qualified variant as a compile-time constant expression.

title: std::variant<Types...>::visit
summary: Applies the visitor vis (a Callable that can be called with any combination of types from the variant) to the variant held by self.

title: std::visit
summary: Applies the visitor v (a Callable that can be called with any combination of types from Variants) to the Variants values.

title: std::variant<Types...>::~variant
summary: If valueless_by_exception() is true, does nothing. Otherwise, destroys the currently contained object.

title: std::weak_order
summary: Compares two values using 3-way comparison and produces a result of type std::weak_ordering.
